subproblems.title: Top-dimensional integer multiplicity currents have an integer-valued L¹_loc density (Lemma A)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, V ⊆ ℝⁿ open and X ∈ 𝒟_n(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V n) integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity X). Let e = (e₁, …, eₙ) be the standard basis of ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ) and, for an n-covector α, write α(e) := α(e₁, …, eₙ). Then there is g : ℝⁿ → ℤ such that y ↦ (g(y) : ℝ) is locally Lebesgue-integrable on V (LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume) and X(ω) = ∫_{ℝⁿ} g(y)·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) (TestFormOn V n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn V n), 0 < n → IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → ∃ g : Euclid n → ℤ, LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, X ω = ∫ y, (g y : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n) y ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma A (step 1) of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero — the density part of the Constancy Theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 2.34, chapter-06.txt lines 571–600), specialized to integer multiplicity currents — with all details filled in. No sibling is used.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] and Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n; Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n gives Hⁿ = Lⁿ. b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ (an orthonormal basis), e := ⇑b, and D := b.toBasis.det, the alternating n-linear form with D(e) = 1 (Module.Basis.det_self). D is continuous (D(v) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of v, Module.Basis.det_apply, a continuous function of v by Continuous.matrix_det), so D defines an n-covector e* ∈ Covector (Euclid n) n with e*(v) = D(v) and e*(e) = 1.
1. Fix R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep V n with R.Represents X (definition of IsIntegerMultiplicity). Thus X(ω) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn V n (IMRep.action); M is a measurable subset of V; θ : ℝⁿ → ℕ is measurable with ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V (field locallyIntegrable_mult); ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Every n-covector α satisfies α(v) = α(e)·D(v) for all v : Fin n → ℝⁿ: apply Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det to the alternating map underlying α and the basis b.toBasis.
3. Let y ∈ M be a point at which the `orients` property of R holds (this is the case for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y): there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q. The first gives finrank Q = n (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq) = finrank ℝⁿ, so Q = ⊤ (Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq). The second gives an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝⁿ with span(range τ) = Q = ⊤ such that either ξ(y)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(y)(α) = −α(τ) for all α. Since τ is orthonormal and spans ⊤, it is an orthonormal basis (OrthonormalBasis.mk with OrthonormalBasis.coe_mk), and the change-of-basis determinant between two orthonormal bases is ±1 (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real); thus D(τ) = b.toBasis.det τ ∈ {1, −1}. By step 2, α(τ) = α(e)·D(τ). Hence there is s(y) ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(y)(α) = s(y)·α(e) for every α; taking α = e* gives s(y) = ξ(y)(e*).
4. Define σ : ℝⁿ → ℝ by σ(y) := ξ(y)(e*). By step 3, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y: σ(y) ∈ {1, −1} and ξ(y)(α) = σ(y)·α(e) for every n-covector α. σ is the composition of ξ with the continuous linear map "evaluation at e*" (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ e*), hence AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M; let σ̃ be a measurable function with σ̃ = σ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk).
5. Define g : ℝⁿ → ℤ by g(y) := θ(y) if y ∈ M and σ̃(y) ≥ 0; g(y) := −θ(y) if y ∈ M and σ̃(y) < 0; g(y) := 0 if y ∉ M. Then g is measurable (M and {σ̃ ≥ 0} are measurable sets, θ is measurable), g = 0 outside M, |g(y)| ≤ θ(y)·1_M(y) for every y, and for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y we have σ̃(y) = σ(y) ∈ {1, −1}, hence (g(y) : ℝ) = θ(y)·σ(y).
6. Local integrability. For a compact K ⊆ V: ∫⁻_K |g| dLⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_K θ·1_M dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (step 5, Hⁿ = Lⁿ, step 1); with the measurability of g, g is integrable on every compact subset of V. Since V is open (hence locally closed), integrability on every compact subset of V is equivalent to LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume (locallyIntegrableOn_iff with hV.isLocallyClosed).
7. Formula. Let ω ∈ TestFormOn V n. For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y, steps 4–5 give θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) = θ(y)·σ(y)·ω(y)(e) = g(y)·ω(y)(e). Hence X(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_M g·ω(e) dHⁿ (integral_congr_ae for Hⁿ⌞M; no integrability is needed for this step). Because g = 0 outside M, ∫_M g·ω(e) dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} g·ω(e) dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), and Hⁿ = Lⁿ turns this into X(ω) = ∫ g(y)·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y). Together with step 6 this proves the statement. ∎
Implementation note (not part of the proof): name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_top_density_ (for example dtc_bc_cz_top_density_aux), because the candidates of sibling children are merged into one Submission.lean and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped during that merge.
proof_key_steps: Fix a representation (M, θ, ξ) of X; the approximate tangent space of M ⊆ ℝⁿ is ℝⁿ, so a.e. ξ(y) = ±e₁∧…∧eₙ (orthonormal n-frames have determinant ±1): ξ(y)(α) = σ(y)α(e) with σ(y) = ξ(y)(e*) ∈ {±1}.
g := θ·sign(σ̃)·1_M (σ̃ a measurable version of σ) is ℤ-valued, measurable and |g| ≤ θ1_M, so g ∈ L¹_loc(V) by locallyIntegrable_mult (Hⁿ = Lⁿ).
X(ω) = ∫_M θξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_M gω(e) dHⁿ = ∫ g ω(e) dLⁿ (a.e. equality on M, g = 0 off M, Hⁿ = Lⁿ).

Then there is c ∈ ℤ such that X(ω) = c·∫_{ℝⁿ} ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ B, where e = (e₁, …, eₙ) is the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun) — i.e. X = c[[B]] in B with the standard orientation.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma B (step 2) of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero, i.e. Simon's proof of the Constancy Theorem (Ch. 6, 2.34, chapter-06.txt lines 571–600: the forms ω_j = (−1)^{j−1} a dx¹∧…∧dx^{j−1}∧dx^{j+1}∧…∧dxⁿ with dω_j = D_j a dx¹∧…∧dxⁿ, and (2) ∫ D_j a·θ dLⁿ = T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0), with Simon's Riesz-representation step replaced by the integer density of sibling top_density, and the parent's mollification step supplied by sibling smooth_to_c1_tests. Siblings used: top_density (A) and smooth_to_c1_tests (S2C = the accepted declaration dgcr_smooth_tests_to_C1_tests). Cited library theorem (pinned SimonGMT, Chapter08/DistributionalConstancy.lean, standard axioms only; add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.DistributionalConstancy`, as accepted candidates in this run already do): Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero — if f : Euclidean n → ℝ (Euclidean n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) = Euclid n) is LocallyIntegrableOn U volume, U is open and preconnected, and ∫ f(x)·fderiv ℝ φ x ((EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ) i) dx = 0 for every φ with ContDiff ℝ 1 φ, HasCompactSupport φ, tsupport φ ⊆ U and every i : Fin n, then ∃ c, ∀ᵐ x ∂volume.restrict U, f x = c.
Notation: e := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ); e* is the n-covector v ↦ D(v), D := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det (continuous because D(v) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of v: Module.Basis.det_apply, Continuous.matrix_det; e*(e) = 1 by Module.Basis.det_self); for k : Fin n, Fin.removeNth k e : Fin m → ℝⁿ is e with its k-th entry removed.
1. By A (n = m + 1 > 0, V open, X integer multiplicity) there is g : ℝⁿ → ℤ, with y ↦ (g(y) : ℝ) locally integrable on V, such that X(ω) = ∫ g(y)·ω(y)(e) dy for every ω ∈ TestFormOn V n.
2. Coordinate m-covectors. For i : Fin n let γ_i := (−1)^i·(e*.curryLeft e_i) ∈ Covector (Euclid n) m, where e*.curryLeft e_i is the contraction w ↦ e*(Matrix.vecCons e_i w) = e*(e_i, w₁, …, w_m) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft, curryLeft_apply_apply). By Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_insertNth (the continuous version of AlternatingMap.map_insertNth), e*(Fin.insertNth i e_i w) = (−1)^i·e*(Matrix.vecCons e_i w); since (−1)^i·(−1)^i = 1, γ_i(w) = e*(Fin.insertNth i e_i w) for all w : Fin m → ℝⁿ. Key identity: γ_i(Fin.removeNth k e) = δ_{ik} for all k : Fin n. For k = i: Fin.insertNth i e_i (Fin.removeNth i e) = e (Fin.insertNth_self_removeNth), so the value is e*(e) = 1. For k ≠ i: there is z : Fin m with k.succAbove z = i (Fin.exists_succAbove_eq), so (Fin.removeNth k e)(z) = e(k.succAbove z) = e_i (Fin.removeNth_apply); the tuple Fin.insertNth i e_i (Fin.removeNth k e) therefore has the entry e_i at position i (Fin.insertNth_apply_same) and at position i.succAbove z (Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove), and i.succAbove z ≠ i (Fin.succAbove_ne); so e* vanishes on it (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq).
3. Let a : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) a, which is SimonGMT's smoothness exponent ∞) with compact support and tsupport a ⊆ B, and let i : Fin n. Put β_i(y) := a(y)·γ_i (a form of degree m). Then β_i is C^∞ (a smooth scalar function times a constant covector), tsupport β_i ⊆ tsupport a (tsupport_smul_subset_left), which is compact and contained in B ⊆ V; so β_i ∈ TestFormOn V m with tsupport β_i ⊆ B.
4. Exterior derivative. By SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply (Mathlib extDeriv_apply), for every y: dβ_i(y)(e) = Σ_{k : Fin n} (−1)^k·D[z ↦ β_i(z)(Fin.removeNth k e)](y)(e_k). Since β_i(z)(Fin.removeNth k e) = a(z)·γ_i(Fin.removeNth k e) = δ_{ik}·a(z) by step 2, the k-th term is (−1)^k·δ_{ik}·Da(y)(e_k); hence dβ_i(y)(e) = (−1)^i·∂_i a(y), where ∂_i a(y) := fderiv ℝ a y (e_i).
5. As tsupport β_i ⊆ B, the hypothesis gives 0 = X.boundary β_i = X(dβ_i) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply: the test form exteriorDerivativeTestOn V m β_i has underlying form dβ_i). By steps 1 and 4, X(dβ_i) = ∫ g(y)·dβ_i(y)(e) dy = (−1)^i·∫ g(y)·∂_i a(y) dy (MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul). Hence ∫ g·∂_i a = 0 for every such a and every i.
6. Constancy. Put G(y) := (g(y) : ℝ); G is LocallyIntegrableOn B (LocallyIntegrableOn.mono_set, B ⊆ V). Apply S2C with D := B (open) and G. Its hypothesis asks, for every a with ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) a, compact support and tsupport a ⊆ B, and every j : Fin n, that ∫_B G·fderiv ℝ a v (EuclideanSpace.single j 1) dv = 0. Here EuclideanSpace.single j 1 = e_j (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), and the integrand vanishes outside tsupport a ⊆ B (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport), so the integral over B equals the integral over ℝⁿ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), which is 0 by step 5. Hence S2C gives ∫ G(x)·fderiv ℝ φ x (e_i) dx = 0 for every C¹ function φ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ B and every i. The library theorem (f := G, U := B, open and preconnected) yields c₀ ∈ ℝ with G = c₀ Lⁿ-a.e. on B.
7. Integrality. If B = ∅ put c := 0. Otherwise B is a nonempty open set, so volume B > 0 (IsOpen.measure_pos), and Measure.exists_mem_of_measure_ne_zero_of_ae (with μ := volume, s := B, applied to the statement ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume.restrict B), G y = c₀) gives y₀ ∈ B with g(y₀) = c₀; put c := g(y₀) ∈ ℤ, so (c : ℝ) = c₀. In both cases G(y) = c for Lⁿ-a.e. y ∈ B (vacuously if B = ∅, as volume.restrict ∅ = 0).
8. Formula. Let ω ∈ TestFormOn V n with tsupport ω ⊆ B. For a.e. y: if y ∈ B then g(y) = c (ae_restrict_iff' with B measurable); if y ∉ B then y ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence g(y)·ω(y)(e) = c·ω(y)(e) for a.e. y, and step 1 gives X(ω) = ∫ g·ω(e) = ∫ c·ω(e) = c·∫ ω(y)(e) dy (integral_congr_ae, MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul). ∎

The continuous-alternating-map API of step 2 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft, ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_insertNth) is already available after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`; only the library constancy theorem needs the extra `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.DistributionalConstancy`.

For a ∈ C_c^∞(B) and the coordinate m-covectors γ_i = (−1)^i e*.curryLeft e_i (γ_i(removeNth k e) = δ_ik), β_i = aγ_i ∈ 𝒟^m(V) has dβ_i(e) = (−1)^i ∂_i a, so 0 = ∂X(β_i) = (−1)^i ∫ g ∂_i a.

subproblems.title: The integer multiplicity current c[[ℝⁿ]]
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and c ∈ ℤ. Then there is C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) which is integer multiplicity and satisfies C(ω) = c·∫_{ℝⁿ} ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ), where e = (e₁, …, eₙ) is the standard basis of ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun) — i.e. C = c[[ℝⁿ]] with the standard orientation e₁∧…∧eₙ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : ℤ), 0 < n → ∃ C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity C ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n, C ω = (c : ℝ) * ∫ y, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n) y ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero (the limit C = c[[ℝⁿ]], its continuity and its integer multiplicity representation), with details filled in. No sibling is used.
Notation: e := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ) (orthonormal, ‖e_i‖ = 1), Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ := volume; Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. For ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n put F_ω(y) := ω(y)(e). F_ω is continuous (ω is smooth, in particular continuous, and evaluation of a continuous alternating map at the fixed tuple e is a continuous linear map) and vanishes outside tsupport ω, which is compact; hence F_ω is continuous with compact support and Lⁿ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). Moreover |F_ω(y)| ≤ ‖ω(y)‖·∏_i ‖e_i‖ = ‖ω(y)‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
2. Define Λ(ω) := c·∫ F_ω dLⁿ. Since F_{ω+η} = F_ω + F_η and F_{tω} = t·F_ω, and these functions are integrable (step 1), Λ is ℝ-linear (integral_add, integral_smul): Λ : TestFormOn univ n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
3. Continuity (the field continuous' of GeometricCurrentOn). Let (ω_q) satisfy TestFormOnConverges ω_q 0: there is a compact K with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for all q, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_q → iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 = 0 uniformly on K. As ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f y‖ = ‖f y‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every ε > 0 and all large q we have ‖ω_q(y)‖ ≤ ε for y ∈ K, while ω_q(y) = 0 for y ∉ K. By step 1, |Λ(ω_q)| ≤ |c|·∫_K ‖ω_q(y)‖ dy ≤ |c|·Lⁿ(K)·ε for all large q, and Lⁿ(K) < ∞ since K is compact. Hence Λ(ω_q) → 0. Thus C := ⟨Λ, continuity⟩ ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n, and C(ω) = c·∫ ω(y)(e) dy.
4. Integer multiplicity, case c = 0. Then C(ω) = 0 for all ω. Let R₀ have carrier ∅, mult ≡ 0 and orient ≡ 0. The IMRep fields hold: ∅ is measurable and ∅ ⊆ univ; CountablyRectifiable n ∅ (Chapter03 countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, Hⁿ(∅) = 0); constant functions are measurable and AEStronglyMeasurable; mult_pos is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅∩K} 0 dHⁿ = 0 ≠ ∞; Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, so the `orients` property holds Hⁿ⌞∅-a.e. R₀.action ω = ∫ over ∅ = 0 = C(ω), so R₀ represents C.
5. Integer multiplicity, case c ≠ 0. Let ε : MultiVector n n = (Covector (Euclid n) n →L[ℝ] ℝ) be the evaluation α ↦ α(e); it is linear and |α(e)| ≤ ‖α‖ (step 1), so it is a continuous linear map (LinearMap.mkContinuous with constant 1). Let s := Int.sign c ∈ {1, −1}, so |c|·s = c. Define R with carrier univ, mult y := c.natAbs = |c| ≥ 1 and orient y := s·ε for all y. Fields: (a) univ is measurable and univ ⊆ univ. (b) CountablyRectifiable n univ: univ = range(id) and id : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Euclid n is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.id), so Chapter03 countablyRectifiable_range applies. (c) mult is constant (measurable) and positive because c ≠ 0. (d) For compact K: ∫⁻_{univ∩K} |c| dHⁿ = |c|·Hⁿ(K) = |c|·Lⁿ(K) < ∞. (e) orient is constant, hence AEStronglyMeasurable. (f) For every y: Q := ⊤ has finrank ⊤ = finrank ℝⁿ = n (finrank_top, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin); Chapter03 hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule (P := ⊤, y ∈ ⊤) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ↑⊤ y ⊤, and ↑(⊤ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid n)) = univ is the carrier (Submodule.top_coe). IsUnitOrientationOf (s·ε) ⊤ holds with τ := e: e is orthonormal (OrthonormalBasis.orthonormal), span(range e) = ⊤ (a basis spans), and (s·ε)(α) = α(e) for every α if c > 0, (s·ε)(α) = −α(e) for every α if c < 0. So `orients` holds at every y, in particular a.e.
6. Action: R.action ω = ∫_{univ} |c|·s·ω(y)(e) dHⁿ(y) = c·∫ ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) = C(ω) (Measure.restrict_univ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ, |c|·s = c, MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul). So R represents C and C is integer multiplicity. ∎
Implementation note (not part of the proof): name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_unit_current_ (for example dtc_bc_cz_unit_current_aux), because the candidates of sibling children are merged into one Submission.lean and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped during that merge.
proof_key_steps: Λ(ω) = c∫ω(e) dLⁿ is linear, and continuous for the test-form topology since |Λ(ω_q)| ≤ |c|Lⁿ(K) sup_K‖ω_q‖ → 0.

c = 0: the empty representation; c ≠ 0: carrier ℝⁿ (range of the 1-Lipschitz identity), multiplicity |c|, orientation sign(c)·(α ↦ α(e)), tangent space ⊤ at every point (hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule) oriented by the orthonormal basis e.
Its action is ∫|c| sign(c) ω(e) dHⁿ = c∫ω(e) dLⁿ = C(ω).

subproblems.title: Blow-ups of a current equal to c[[ℝⁿ]] on a ball, and of local boundary vanishing
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝⁿ, ρ, c ∈ ℝ and λ > 0 with B_ρ(x) ⊆ U; let η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ (η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x)) and S := η_{x,λ#}T = blowUp T x λ ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)); e = standard basis of ℝⁿ. (i) If T(ω) = c·∫ω(y)(e) dy for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ(x), then currentEval(S, ω) = c·∫ω(z)(e) dz for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0). (ii) If ∂T(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ(x), then ∂S(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(η(U)) with tsupport β ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (x : Euclid (m + 1)) (ρ c lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam), ball x ρ ⊆ U → ((∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball x ρ → T ω = c * ∫ y, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) y ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball 0 (ρ / lam) → currentEval (blowUp T x lam hlam.ne') (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) = c * ∫ z, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) z ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ)) ∧ ((∀ β : TestFormOn U m, tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) m) ⊆ ball x ρ → T.boundary β = 0) → ∀ β : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) m, tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) m) ⊆ ball 0 (ρ / lam) → (blowUp T x lam hlam.ne').boundary β = 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero (the blow-ups agree with c[[ℝⁿ]] on the balls B_{ρ/λ}(0) by the change of variables y = x + λz; ∂S = ∂T(η^#·) vanishes there), with details filled in. No sibling is used.
Notation: e := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ); L := dilationCLM n λ = λ⁻¹·id; b := −(λ⁻¹·x); η(y) := dilation x λ y = b + L y = λ⁻¹(y − x). For a k-form ω on ℝⁿ, η^#ω := affinePullbackForm L b ω, (η^#ω)(y) = ω(η(y)) ∘ L, i.e. (η^#ω)(y)(v₁, …, v_k) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁, …, λ⁻¹v_k).
1. Unfolding blowUp. By definition blowUp T x λ = (T.restrictDomain h).affinePushforward L b hproper, with h : η⁻¹(η(U)) ⊆ U. By GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply and GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply, for every ω ∈ TestFormOn (η(U)) n: S(ω) = T(ω♯), where ω♯ ∈ TestFormOn U n is the test form whose underlying form is η^#ω (affinePullbackTestOn followed by testFormOnInclusion h).
2. Balls. η is a bijection of ℝⁿ with inverse z ↦ x + λz, and ‖η(y)‖ = λ⁻¹‖y − x‖. Hence η⁻¹(B_{ρ/λ}(0)) = B_ρ(x) and η(B_ρ(x)) = B_{ρ/λ}(0); in particular B_{ρ/λ}(0) ⊆ η(U).
3. Supports. tsupport(η^#ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset). So tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0) implies tsupport(η^#ω) ⊆ B_ρ(x).
4. Pullback on e. By multilinearity, (η^#ω)(y)(e) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹e₁, …, λ⁻¹eₙ) = λ^{−n}·ω(η(y))(e) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ; ∏_{i<n} λ⁻¹ = λ^{−n}).
5. Change of variables. For F : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ∫ F(η(y)) dy = λⁿ·∫ F(z) dz: F(η(y)) = F(λ⁻¹·(y − x)); translation invariance of Lebesgue measure (integral_sub_right_eq_self) gives ∫ F(λ⁻¹(y − x)) dy = ∫ F(λ⁻¹y) dy, and Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul_of_nonneg (λ ≥ 0; finrank ℝⁿ = n by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) gives ∫ F(λ⁻¹y) dy = λⁿ·∫ F(z) dz. (No integrability assumption is needed.)
6. Proof of (i). Let ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0). Then ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ η(U) (step 2), so by the definition of currentEval (its dite condition holds) currentEval(S, ω) = S(ω'), where ω' ∈ TestFormOn (η(U)) n has underlying form ω. By step 1, S(ω') = T(ω'♯), and the underlying form η^#ω of ω'♯ has tsupport ⊆ B_ρ(x) (step 3). By the hypothesis of (i), then step 4 and step 5 with F(z) := ω(z)(e): T(ω'♯) = c·∫ (η^#ω)(y)(e) dy = c·λ^{−n}·∫ ω(η(y))(e) dy = c·λ^{−n}·λⁿ·∫ ω(z)(e) dz = c·∫ ω(z)(e) dz.
7. Proof of (ii). Let β ∈ TestFormOn (η(U)) m with tsupport β ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0). By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, ∂S(β) = S(β₁), where β₁ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn (η(U)) m β has underlying form dβ. By step 1, S(β₁) = T(ζ), where ζ ∈ TestFormOn U n has underlying form η^#(dβ). By SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm, η^#(dβ) = d(η^#β); hence ζ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m β♯, where β♯ ∈ TestFormOn U m has underlying form η^#β (equality of test forms by Subtype.ext). [Equivalently: GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward, plus the fact that boundary commutes with restrictDomain, which holds by definition.] Thus ∂S(β) = T(dβ♯) = ∂T(β♯). Finally tsupport(η^#β) ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport β) ⊆ B_ρ(x) (step 3), so ∂T(β♯) = 0 by the hypothesis of (ii). ∎
Implementation note (not part of the proof): name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_blowUp_eval_ (for example dtc_bc_cz_blowUp_eval_aux), because the candidates of sibling children are merged into one Submission.lean and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped during that merge. Lean hint: after unfolding blowUp, the simp lemmas testFormOnInclusion_coe / affinePullbackTestOn_coe may not fire on the nested coercions; a `change` to the explicit expression T ⟨affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM (m + 1) lam) (-(lam⁻¹ • x)) ω, _⟩ works (the two sides are definitionally equal).
proof_key_steps: blowUp T x λ = (T.restrictDomain _).affinePushforward L b _, so S(ω) = T(η^#ω) with η^#ω(y)(e) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y))(e) and tsupport η^#ω ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω).
η⁻¹(B_{ρ/λ}(0)) = B_ρ(x), so forms supported in B_{ρ/λ}(0) pull back to forms supported in B_ρ(x) ⊆ U.
(i): T(η^#ω) = cλ^{−n}∫ω(λ⁻¹(y − x))(e)dy = c∫ω(z)(e)dz by translation and Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul_of_nonneg.
(ii): ∂S(β) = T(η^#dβ) = T(d η^#β) = ∂T(η^#β) = 0 (exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm).

subproblems.title: Every integer multiplicity n-current in ℝⁿ is minimizing
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) integer multiplicity, and A ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set. Then C is minimizing in A (Simon 7.1.1, IsMinimizingIn C A). In fact every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) with ∂S = ∂C and spt(S − C) compact equals C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n) (A : Set (Euclid n)), 0 < n → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → IsMinimizingIn C A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero (minimality of C: a competitor differs from C by a compactly supported integer multiplicity cycle, which the Constancy Theorem forces to vanish), stated for an arbitrary integer multiplicity C and an arbitrary A (the argument never uses spt(S − C) ⊆ A ∩ W). Siblings used: top_constancy (Cst), im_sub (G = the accepted declaration dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub) and vanish_off_support (V = the accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support).
1. Write n = m + 1. The first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn C A is IsIntegerMultiplicity C, a hypothesis.
2. Let W be open with CompactlyContained W univ, and let S ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n be integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S C (for n = m + 1 this unfolds to S.boundary = C.boundary), IsCompact (S − C).support and (S − C).support ⊆ A ∩ W. Put X := S − C; by the definition of subtraction of currents (toCurrent := S.toCurrent − C.toCurrent), X(ω) = S(ω) − C(ω) for every ω.
3. X is integer multiplicity by G (univ is open, n > 0, S and C are integer multiplicity).
4. ∂X = 0: for β ∈ TestFormOn univ m, X.boundary β = X(dβ) = S(dβ) − C(dβ) = S.boundary β − C.boundary β = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).
5. Apply Cst with V := B := univ (open; preconnected since ℝⁿ is convex, convex_univ.isPreconnected), X (step 3) and the hypothesis of step 4: there is c' ∈ ℤ with X(ω) = c'·∫ ω(y)(e) dy for every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n (the condition tsupport ω ⊆ univ is automatic).
6. c' = 0. The set spt X = (S − C).support is compact, hence bounded: spt X ⊆ closedBall(0, r₀) for some r₀ ∈ ℝ (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Let p := (|r₀| + 2)·e₁ (n ≥ 1; ‖p‖ = |r₀| + 2 since ‖e₁‖ = 1), and let a be the smooth bump function centred at p with inner radius 1/2 and outer radius 1 (ContDiffBump p): a is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), a ≥ 0, HasCompactSupport a, tsupport a = closedBall(p, 1) (ContDiffBump.tsupport_eq), and ∫ a > 0 (ContDiffBump.integral_pos, from Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed). Let e* be the n-covector v ↦ D(v), D := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det (continuous because D(v) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of v: Module.Basis.det_apply, Continuous.matrix_det; e*(e) = 1 by Module.Basis.det_self), and ω(y) := a(y)·e*. Then ω is smooth with compact support, so ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n, and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport a = closedBall(p, 1) (tsupport_smul_subset_left). For y ∈ closedBall(p, 1), ‖y‖ ≥ ‖p‖ − ‖y − p‖ ≥ |r₀| + 1 > r₀, so tsupport ω is disjoint from closedBall(0, r₀) ⊇ spt X, and V gives X(ω) = 0. By step 5, X(ω) = c'·∫ a(y)·e*(e) dy = c'·∫ a. Since ∫ a > 0, c' = 0.
7. Hence X(ω) = 0, i.e. S(ω) = C(ω), for every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n; so S = C (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), C.massOn W = S.massOn W, and in particular C.massOn W ≤ S.massOn W. This proves IsMinimizingIn C A. ∎
Implementation note (not part of the proof): name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_isMinimizingIn_ (for example dtc_bc_cz_isMinimizingIn_aux), because the candidates of sibling children are merged into one Submission.lean and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped during that merge. ContDiffBump.integral_pos needs `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed`, which is outside the frozen import closure.
proof_key_steps: A competitor S gives the integer multiplicity cycle X = S − C (im_sub; ∂X = ∂S − ∂C = 0) with compact support.
top_constancy on V = B = ℝⁿ gives X = c'[[ℝⁿ]].
Testing X with a·e*, a ≥ 0 a bump supported away from spt X with ∫a > 0, gives 0 = X(a e*) = c'∫a (vanish_off_support), so c' = 0, S = C and M_W(C) = M_W(S).

subproblems.title: Eventual agreement on balls gives weak convergence, convergence of mass measures and ∂C = 0
subproblems.statement: Assume measure locality (MEAS, the exact type of dtc_bc_measure_restrict_eq_of_eqOn, taken as a hypothesis): for all P, n, open U₁, U₂, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂, T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U₁), T₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(U₂) and integer multiplicity representations R₁ of T₁, R₂ of T₂, if currentEval T₁ ω = currentEval T₂ ω for every ω ∈ TestFormOn W n then R₁.measure.restrict W = R₂.measure.restrict W. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U_j ⊆ ℝ^P open (j ∈ ℕ), S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Choose R₀ with tsupport f ⊆ W := B_{R₀}(0) (step 0), and let j be large enough that the hypothesis holds with R := R₀. 1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.

3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.

A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756, stated without proof). Tools: the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 700–722; SimonGMT Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean), and the fact that approximate tangent spaces only depend on a set up to sets of zero density, Ch. 3, 1.4–1.5 and Remark 1.8(1) (chapter-03.txt lines 77–108, 298–310). Throughout Hⁿ = μHE[n], η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap), and Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(E)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for all E (μHE[n] is translation invariant and n-homogeneous: Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁) and R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be IMReps in U representing S and T.
1. Local finiteness. For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M_i∩K} θ_i dHⁿ < ∞ since θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i. Hence every Borel A ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ has Hⁿ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U.
2. (F1) If A ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ is Borel, then ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ U ∖ A. Proof: let V_j be open sets with compact closures in U and ⋃_j V_j = U; apply Ch. 1, 3.6 to the finite Borel-regular measure Hⁿ⌞(A ∩ V_j) to get the conclusion for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ V_j ∖ A (for y ∈ V_j and small ρ, B_ρ(y) ⊆ V_j), and take the union of the countably many exceptional null sets.
3. (F2) Let A, A' be Hⁿ-measurable, y ∈ U, s > 0 with Hⁿ(A ∩ B_s(y)), Hⁿ(A' ∩ B_s(y)) < ∞, ρ^{−n}Hⁿ((A Δ A') ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0, and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A y Q. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A' y Q. Proof: finrank Q = n is unchanged. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_L(0) and 0 < r < s/L both blow-up integrals are finite and |∫_{η_{y,r}(A')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·Hⁿ(η_{y,r}(A Δ A') ∩ B_L(0)) = sup|f|·r^{−n}Hⁿ((A Δ A') ∩ B_{Lr}(y)) → 0, so the blow-up integrals of A' converge to ∫_Q f dHⁿ as well.
4. (F3) If ζ and ζ' are both unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q (IsUnitOrientationOf), then ζ' = ±ζ: if ζ(α) = σα(τ) and ζ'(α) = σ'α(τ') with τ, τ' orthonormal bases of Q, then τ' = τB for an orthogonal n×n matrix B, and multilinearity plus the alternating property give α(τ') = det(B)α(τ) with det B = ±1.
5. Normalization. Changing ξ_i on an Hⁿ⌞M_i-null set changes neither the integrals in R_i.Represents nor the almost-everywhere statement `orients`; so we may assume ξ₁, ξ₂ Borel measurable. Put E := M₁ ∩ M₂. For increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P} let e^I ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) be the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; these form a basis of Λⁿ(ℝ^P), so an n-vector ζ (a linear functional on Λⁿ) is determined by the numbers ζ(e^I). If ζ(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal frame τ, then ζ ≠ 0 (the covector (v₁,…,vₙ) ↦ det(⟨τ_a, v_b⟩) takes the value ±1 under ζ), hence Σ_I ζ(e^I)² > 0.
6. Common tangent planes. For Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M_i the approximate tangent space T_yM_i exists and ξ_i(y) orients it. By F1 (with A = M₁ ∖ M₂ and A = M₂ ∖ M₁) and F2 (with A = M_i, A' = E, since M_i Δ E ⊆ M₁ ∖ M₂ or ⊆ M₂ ∖ M₁ and y ∉ these sets), for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ E the space T_yE exists and T_yM₁ = T_yE = T_yM₂. By F3, for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ E, ξ₂(y) = σ'ξ₁(y) for some σ' ∈ {±1}; then Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)ξ₂(y)(e^I) = σ'Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)² with Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)² > 0 (step 5), so σ' = σ(y) := sign(Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)·ξ₂(y)(e^I)), a Borel function, and ξ₂(y) = σ(y)ξ₁(y). The set of points of E where any of these properties fails is Hⁿ-null, hence contained in a Borel null set; let G ⊆ E be the Borel complement of that null set in E.
7. New data. On G put d := θ₁ − σθ₂ ∈ ℤ and G' := {y ∈ G : d(y) ≠ 0}. Define the Borel set M := (M₁ ∖ M₂) ∪ (M₂ ∖ M₁) ∪ G', the measurable m : ℝ^P → ℕ with m = θ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, m = θ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, m = |d| on G', m = 0 elsewhere, and the Borel ζ with ζ = ξ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, ζ = −ξ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, ζ = sign(d)ξ₁ on G', ζ = 0 elsewhere.
8. IMRep fields. M ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ ⊆ U; M is countably n-rectifiable (subset of the union of two countably n-rectifiable sets: SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono, countablyRectifiable_iUnion); m ≥ 1 on M; m ≤ θ₁1_{M₁} + θ₂1_{M₂} (on G', |d| ≤ θ₁ + θ₂), so ∫_{M∩K} m dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M₁∩K} θ₁ + ∫_{M₂∩K} θ₂ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Orientation property for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M: (i) y ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂: M Δ M₁ ⊆ M₂ and, by F1 with A = M₂, M₂ has density 0 at a.e. y ∉ M₂, so F2 gives T_yM = T_yM₁, oriented by ξ₁(y) = ζ(y); (ii) y ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁: symmetrically T_yM = T_yM₂, oriented by ξ₂(y) and hence by ζ(y) = −ξ₂(y) (IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign); (iii) y ∈ G': M Δ M₁ = (M₂ ∖ M₁) ∪ (E ∖ G') is a Borel set not containing y, so by F1 it has density 0 at a.e. such y, and F2 gives T_yM = T_yM₁, oriented by ξ₁(y) and hence by ζ(y) = ±ξ₁(y).
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (all integrands are integrable, being bounded by (θ₁1_{M₁} + θ₂1_{M₂})·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}): (S − T)(ω) = ∫_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁(ω) − ∫_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂(ω) = ∫_{M₁∖M₂}θ₁ξ₁(ω) + ∫_{M₂∖M₁}θ₂(−ξ₂)(ω) + ∫_E (θ₁ξ₁ − θ₂ξ₂)(ω) dHⁿ. On G, θ₁ξ₁ − θ₂ξ₂ = (θ₁ − σθ₂)ξ₁ = |d|·sign(d)ξ₁, which vanishes on G ∖ G', and E ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; so the last integral equals ∫_{G'} |d| sign(d)ξ₁(ω) dHⁿ. Hence (S − T)(ω) = ∫_M m ζ(ω) dHⁿ, i.e. (M, m, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing S − T, and S − T is integer multiplicity.
proof_key_steps: Upper Density Theorem: a set of locally finite Hⁿ-measure has density zero at Hⁿ-a.e. point outside it.
Approximate tangent spaces are unchanged by modifications of density zero, so on M₁ ∩ M₂ the tangent planes agree a.e. and ξ₂ = ±ξ₁.
Combine carriers: M₁∖M₂, M₂∖M₁ and the part of M₁∩M₂ where θ₁ξ₁ ≠ θ₂ξ₂, with integer multiplicities |θ₁ ∓ θ₂| and signed orientations.
Verify every IMRep field and the representation identity for S − T.

Mathlib's normalized-bump API (ContDiffBump.normed, BumpFunction.Convolution) is NOT in the frozen import closure, so the mollifier is normalized by hand below; all lemmas cited are in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.
1. Fix φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ D, and fix i. (If n = 0 there is no index i; assume n ≥ 1.) K := tsupport φ is compact and K ⊆ D; choose δ > 0 with K_δ := cthickening δ K ⊆ D (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); K_δ is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). G is integrable on K_δ (LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset with K_δ ⊆ D).
2. Mollifiers. For r > 0 let B_r be a ContDiffBump centred at 0 ∈ ℝⁿ with rIn = r/2 and rOut = r; as a function ℝⁿ → ℝ it is smooth (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ B_r ≤ 1, B_r = 1 on B̄_{r/2}(0), and support B_r = B_r(0) (ContDiffBump.support_eq), so it is continuous with compact support and integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). I_r := ∫ B_r > 0 by integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, since B_r ≥ 0 and its support, the open ball B_r(0), has positive Lebesgue measure (Metric.measure_ball_pos). Put ϱ_r := I_r⁻¹·B_r. Then ϱ_r is smooth with compact support, ϱ_r ≥ 0, ∫ϱ_r = 1 (integral_smul / integral_const_mul), and support ϱ_r ⊆ B_r(0).
3. For ℓ ∈ ℕ put r_ℓ := δ/(ℓ+1) and φ_ℓ := ϱ_{r_ℓ} ⋆ φ.
 (a) φ_ℓ is smooth: HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left (ϱ_{r_ℓ} smooth with compact support, φ continuous hence locally integrable), with order (⊤ : ℕ∞).
 (b) support φ_ℓ ⊆ support ϱ_{r_ℓ} + support φ ⊆ B_{r_ℓ}(0) + K (MeasureTheory.support_convolution_subset) ⊆ thickening r_ℓ K ⊆ cthickening δ K = K_δ, a closed set; hence tsupport φ_ℓ ⊆ K_δ ⊆ D and φ_ℓ has compact support (closed subset of the compact K_δ; HasCompactSupport.intro).
 (c) Dφ_ℓ = ϱ_{r_ℓ} ⋆ Dφ (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right with φ ∈ C¹ of compact support and ϱ_{r_ℓ} locally integrable; the convolution is taken with the precomposed bilinear map), and evaluating at eᵢ (MeasureTheory.convolution_precompR_apply) gives ∂ᵢφ_ℓ(x) = (ϱ_{r_ℓ} ⋆ ∂ᵢφ)(x) for every x.
 (d) Uniform convergence. ∂ᵢφ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv with one_ne_zero) with compact support (support ⊆ tsupport φ, HasCompactSupport.fderiv), hence uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Given ε > 0 choose r₀ > 0 with |∂ᵢφ(x') − ∂ᵢφ(x)| ≤ ε whenever ‖x' − x‖ < r₀. For ℓ with r_ℓ ≤ r₀ and every x, MeasureTheory.dist_convolution_le (kernel ϱ_{r_ℓ} ≥ 0 pointwise with ∫ϱ_{r_ℓ} = 1 and support in B_{r_ℓ}(0); ∂ᵢφ is AE-strongly measurable; |∂ᵢφ(x') − ∂ᵢφ(x)| ≤ ε for x' ∈ B_{r_ℓ}(x)) gives |∂ᵢφ_ℓ(x) − ∂ᵢφ(x)| ≤ ε for every x.
4. By hypothesis, applied to a := φ_ℓ (smooth, compact support, tsupport ⊆ D) and j := i: ∫_D G·∂ᵢφ_ℓ = 0 for every ℓ.
5. Both ∂ᵢφ and ∂ᵢφ_ℓ vanish outside K_δ (fderiv vanishes outside the topological support, fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport, and tsupport φ, tsupport φ_ℓ ⊆ K_δ). Hence the integrals over D equal the integrals over K_δ (MeasureTheory.setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero with K_δ ⊆ D, both measurable), and all integrands are integrable on K_δ (G integrable on K_δ times a bounded continuous function, Integrable.mul_bdd). Let ε > 0 and take ℓ as in step 3(d). Then by step 4
 |∫_D G·∂ᵢφ| = |∫_{K_δ} G·∂ᵢφ − ∫_{K_δ} G·∂ᵢφ_ℓ| = |∫_{K_δ} G·(∂ᵢφ − ∂ᵢφ_ℓ)| ≤ ε·∫_{K_δ}|G| (MeasureTheory.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). As ε > 0 is arbitrary and ∫_{K_δ}|G| < ∞, ∫_D G·∂ᵢφ = 0.
6. Finally ∫_{ℝⁿ} G·∂ᵢφ = ∫_D G·∂ᵢφ because the integrand vanishes outside tsupport φ ⊆ D (MeasureTheory.setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), so ∫ x, G x * fderiv ℝ φ x (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with K_δ := cthickening δ (tsupport φ) ⊆ D; G is integrable on the compact K_δ.
Hand-normalized smooth mollifiers ϱ_r = (∫B_r)⁻¹B_r (ContDiffBump, support B_r(0), integral 1).
φ_ℓ := ϱ_{r_ℓ} ⋆ φ is smooth, tsupport φ_ℓ ⊆ K_δ ⊆ D, and ∂ᵢφ_ℓ = ϱ_{r_ℓ} ⋆ ∂ᵢφ → ∂ᵢφ uniformly (dist_convolution_le, uniform continuity).
The smooth-test hypothesis gives ∫_D G ∂ᵢφ_ℓ = 0, and |∫_D G ∂ᵢφ| ≤ ε·∫_{K_δ}|G| for every ε > 0, so ∫_D G ∂ᵢφ = 0.
The integrand vanishes off tsupport φ ⊆ D, so the whole-space integral is 0 (the exact hypothesis form of the Chapter 8 constancy theorem).
